preamble: Gliding of the voiced labiodental fricative [v] to the labial-velar approximant [w] (often transcribed [u̯]) in the syllable coda, where the glide forms a falling diphthong with the preceding vowel. It is a feature of the East Slavic dialect continuum: Belarusian pronounces coda /v/ as [w] and writes it ⟨ў⟩, Ukrainian coda /ʋ/ is likewise [u̯] (ви́вчити [ˈʋɪu̯t͡ʃɪtɪ]), and the western and central Southern Russian dialects have the same glide where Standard Russian has [v] or devoiced [f].

examples.note: In the syllable coda /v/ is pronounced [w] or [u̯] and spelled ⟨ў⟩.
The glide replaces the coda labiodental before a consonant.
Where Russian devoices coda /v/ to [f], Belarusian has [w].

The western and central groups of the Southern dialects have bilabial [w] (written ў in dialect transcription) in place of /v/; mapped in the Dialectological Atlas of the Russian Language (1986), map 56.
Word-final /v/ in the genitive plural ending is a glide rather than devoiced [f].
Dialect form recorded alongside за́фтря and за́йтря.

examples.from: ви́вчити /ʋ/ in the coda 'to have learnt'
examples.note: In syllable codas /ʋ/ is most commonly realized as non-syllabic [u̯] (also transcribed [w]).
Word-initial /ʋ/ before a consonant is likewise non-syllabic [u̯] and alternates with syllabic /u/.
